Write a process document for ending a contractor engagement, covering two scenarios:
Scenario A — Project complete, good experience: End-of-project feedback (what to share with them), final payment process, testimonial exchange, how to keep them in your network for future work.
Scenario B — Ending early due to performance issues: How to document concerns, the conversation script for letting them go (direct, honest, kind), final payment obligations, transition of work in progress, protecting confidential information.
For both: include email templates, checklist of items to hand off/recover (logins, files, tools), and a timeline. My business is [describe]. The contractor role is [describe].

Write a long-form sales page for my [digital product — course, template, ebook, etc.] called "[product name]." Price: [price]. Target buyer: [describe them and their current frustration]. The product includes: [list what's inside]. Results people can expect: [describe outcomes].
Structure: (1) Big bold headline — call out the reader and the transformation, (2) "If you're like most [audience]..." — describe their current pain, (3) "What if instead..." — paint the after picture, (4) Introduce the product, (5) What's inside (module breakdown or contents with benefits), (6) Who this is for / who this is NOT for, (7) Testimonials/results (use these: [paste any you have], or write realistic placeholder quotes), (8) Pricing section with anchor comparison ("This would cost $X if you hired someone..."), (9) FAQ (write 6-8 objection-busting questions), (10) Final CTA with urgency or bonus.
